clue.text: Fountain sited in a good position

parts.note: a well is a spring or fountain of water
something sited has been placed

explanation.surface: A drinking fountain has been installed somewhere handy.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone well-placed is advantageously situated, in a favourable spot.

clue.text: Means to change the law

indicators.note: the letters of the words 'the law' are to be changed into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone sets out the methods available for reforming legislation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Means' looks like a verb ('signifies') but is the noun: one's means are one's money.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's means are their financial resources, their riches.

clue.text: Hardy partner comes from the bay

explanation.surface: Someone's comedy partner turns out to hail from a seaside bay.
explanation.walkthrough: Stan Laurel was the partner of Oliver Hardy in the film comedy double act; the bay tree is also called the laurel.
explanation.definitionFit: Stan Laurel partnered Oliver Hardy on screen, and the bay tree used in cooking is the sweet laurel.

clue.text: Used the television clock when in a hurry

explanation.surface: Someone in a rush jabs at the remote to check the time on screen.
explanation.walkthrough: The first reading is literal: you pressed a button to get the time displayed.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally, pushing a button to show the hour; idiomatically, being short of minutes and rushed.

clue.text: Daniel gets assimilated in another nation fairly slowly

indicators.note: being assimilated in something means being absorbed inside it, so one piece goes within the other
another nation is a different arrangement of the same word, so its letters are reordered

parts.note: Dan is the short form of the name Daniel

explanation.surface: A man called Daniel blends in when he moves abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' turns NATION into ANTINO, and 'assimilated in' puts DAN inside it after AN.
explanation.definitionFit: In music this tempo marking means a little quicker than andante, a moderately leisurely pace.

clue.text: Follow directions given by Miss Barker

parts.note: E and N are the compass points east and north, two directions
Sue Barker is a British former tennis player and TV sports presenter

explanation.surface: Someone obeys the instructions issued by a woman named Barker.
explanation.walkthrough: Sue Barker is a well-known British tennis player turned BBC presenter.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensue is to come after, to result as a consequence.

clue.text: Check when there's a dog born

parts.note: a cur is a mongrel dog
b is the standard abbreviation for born in genealogies

explanation.surface: A vet examines a puppy at the moment of its birth.
explanation.definitionFit: To curb something is to restrain or hold it back.

clue.text: No tulips are produced without soil

indicators.note: the letters of 'No tulips' are produced in a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A gardener finds that bulbs won't flower unless they're planted in earth.
explanation.definitionFit: Unspoilt means untouched and clean, unsullied by dirt.

clue.text: Sweet success for the darts player

explanation.surface: A darts player enjoys a lovely moment of triumph.
explanation.walkthrough: A bullseye is a British striped peppermint boiled sweet as well as the centre of a dartboard.
explanation.definitionFit: A hard striped mint is one sense; a hit on the dartboard's centre is the other.

clue.text: Avoiding a take-over by socialising

explanation.surface: A firm fends off a hostile bid by schmoozing.
explanation.definitionFit: Retaining one's firm in a buyout fight, and spending time with friends or courting.

clue.text: A lovely little French accent

parts.note: something small and lovely is cute

explanation.surface: Someone finds a charming touch of Gallic speech endearing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French accent' is not a way of speaking but a written mark, the accent aigu.
explanation.definitionFit: The acute is the rising diacritic over the e in French words such as café.

clue.text: Scattering Diana's pearls all over the place

parts.note: Diana is shortened to Di, and with the possessive gives Di's

indicators.note: the word pearls is scattered all over the place, so its letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A princess's necklace snaps and the beads roll everywhere.
explanation.definitionFit: Dispersal is the spreading out of things in many directions.

clue.text: The leader has cause for crime against the state

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, here of 'The'

parts.note: a reason is a cause

explanation.surface: A rebel chief has motives for plotting against the government.
explanation.definitionFit: Treason is betrayal of one's country, such as plotting to overthrow its ruler.

clue.text: Uses mutton on manoeuvres

parts.note: in printing, an em space was called a mutton to distinguish it from an en (nut)
ploys are tactical manoeuvres

explanation.surface: A shepherd puts his sheep through their paces.
explanation.walkthrough: Printers called the em space a 'mutton', a rare piece of typesetting jargon.
explanation.definitionFit: To employ something is to make use of it.

clue.text: Italian oddly ill-disposed, moreover

indicators.note: read as 'badly arranged', the letters of 'Italian oddly' are set out differently

explanation.surface: An Italian is strangely unfriendly, and what's more...
explanation.definitionFit: Additionally and moreover both introduce a further point, meaning also or besides.

clue.text: Popular prior catches small rats

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
former means prior or earlier
S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: A well-liked monk captures some little rodents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prior' looks like a monastery head, and 'rats' like rodents; here rats are people who tell tales.
explanation.definitionFit: A rat in slang is a snitch who betrays associates to the authorities.

clue.text: Look for gold with a chance of success

explanation.surface: A miner pans for nuggets with some hope of striking it rich.
explanation.definitionFit: To search for mineral deposits, and a likelihood or hope of something happening.

clue.text: Baby Ray doesn't have a set of soldiers

parts.note: an infant is a baby

indicators.note: the name lacks the letter named, so it is removed

parts.note: taken as written, the name Ray

explanation.surface: A little boy named Ray is missing his toy army.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doesn't have a' takes the A out of RAY, leaving RY.
explanation.definitionFit: Infantry are foot soldiers, a body of troops serving on foot.

clue.text: What American candidates do if late for work?

explanation.surface: A question about the habits of tardy US election hopefuls.
explanation.definitionFit: Americans seek election this way where Britons stand, and a late commuter would literally dash to the workplace.

clue.text: I am, unfortunately, upset by sausage

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the letters read from the bottom up

parts.note: I'm is the contraction of 'I am'
alas is an exclamation meaning unfortunately

explanation.surface: Someone is sadly put out by a sausage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns IMALAS (I'M plus ALAS) backwards in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Salami is a cured spiced Italian sausage.

clue.text: Club bearer makes a scoundrel pass on

parts.note: a cad is a dishonourable man
to pass on is a euphemism for to die

explanation.surface: A rogue's death is announced at a society gathering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Club bearer' suggests a caveman; it is golf.
explanation.definitionFit: A golf assistant carries the player's bag of clubs around the course.

clue.text: Old Greek bridge conceals consummate skill

indicators.note: the bridge word conceals the skill word inside it

parts.note: a span is a bridge or arch
art is consummate skill, as in the art of conversation

explanation.surface: An ancient bridge hides a masterly piece of engineering.
explanation.definitionFit: A Spartan was a citizen of Sparta, a city-state of ancient Greece.

clue.text: His nature is too for this world." (Coriolanus',Act III)

definitions.text: His nature is too for this world

parts.words: His nature is too for this world
parts.note: a line from Shakespeare's Coriolanus with its adjective missing, to be supplied from the play

explanation.surface: A quotation from Shakespeare's Coriolanus with a word left out.
explanation.walkthrough: Menenius says of Coriolanus in Act III: his nature is too ___ for this world; the missing word fills the gap.
explanation.definitionFit: The gap takes the adjective meaning high-minded and honourable, as Shakespeare wrote it.

clue.text: Dance graduate has a little cake

parts.note: the rumba is a Cuban ballroom dance
a BA is a Bachelor of Arts, a graduate

explanation.surface: A student at a dance treats themself to a small pastry.
explanation.definitionFit: A rum baba is a small sponge cake soaked in rum syrup.

clue.text: Worthy male best suited to embrace one

indicators.note: the rearranged letters embrace, or wrap around, the single letter
the letters of 'male best' are suited, or fitted, into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: The finest man for the job will win someone's heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suited' rearranges MALEBEST into ESTMABLE, and 'to embrace' puts I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Estimable means deserving respect or esteem.

clue.text: A minor prize

parts.note: a ward is a minor placed under a guardian's care

explanation.surface: A child receives a small trophy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'minor prize' reads as one phrase; split it: 'minor' is the ward and 'prize' the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An award is a prize given in recognition of achievement.

clue.text: Fiddles made for children

explanation.surface: Violins built for kids to play on.
explanation.definitionFit: To toy with something is to fiddle idly with it, and playthings are made for youngsters.

clue.text: Just the place for Everton

parts.note: Everton is a football side from Liverpool, so a team based on the river there is literally a side of that river

explanation.surface: A remark that a football club has found its ideal home.
explanation.walkthrough: Everton is a Liverpool football club; the county is around the River Mersey, so a Mersey side is just the place for a side.
explanation.definitionFit: The metropolitan county around Liverpool is home to the club.
